proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current proposition records only the empirical-correction branch.  The already-proved refined bracket also yields collision-scale risk whenever the rare-cell approximation scale satisfies \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), so the union is a strictly stronger consequence on the unchanged model class.

proposed.name: Residual wedge after the parent endpoints and both collision-scale regions

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened collision proposition closes every point with \(2\le d\le n\) for which either \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\).  The residual set must therefore add the exclusion \(u_{n,d}>n^{-1}\) while retaining all previous restrictions.

The open question names \(\mathcal W\), so its proof spine must depend explicitly on the corrected residual-wedge definition.  The benchmark itself remains outside both newly closed collision-scale branches.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether a supportwise radius-valid, exactly normalized, conditionally centered shared-design marked coupling at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\) can attain \(\rho_n\sqrt n\to\infty\), or prove that every coupling in a precisely specified version of that program has \(\rho_n=O_{\epsilon}(n^{-1/2})\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The construction handle does not define the mark-score class, the latent shared-design law, the admissible hypothesis-dependent couplings, or the conditional likelihood constraints.  Consequently its advertised maximum is not yet a well-defined optimization.  Even under the broader well-defined outer feasibility conditions, the established minimax upper bound yields only a logarithmic upper gap and does not decide the requested dichotomy.
open_obligations.attempted: The exactly normalized balanced-mark global-shift family was tested and fails because its first-order signed-outcome shift drives total variation to one.  A testing reduction from the refined minimax upper bound gives the outer logarithmic upper bound, while an explicit homogeneous singleton-prior pair attains parametric separation and total variation at most one third.  Neither argument controls all latent, conditionally centered shared-design couplings.

prose_updates.tldr: The kernel is the finite-sample minimax MSE frontier for an identified ATE when high-dimensional discrete adjustment cells have effects within a calibrated maximal radius \(\sigma M\) of the ATE.  The exact split-sample empirical-mass estimator gives collision-scale risk \(M^2/n\) for \(2\le d\le n\) when \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\), while the inherited rare-cell approximation branch gives the same rate when \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), equivalently \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\).  Thus approximate common effects retain collision-scale estimation on the union of these two directly checkable regions.  At the still-unresolved benchmark \(d=n\), \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), an exactly normalized shared-design marked family fails because its global outcome shift makes the full mixtures distinguishable; the conditionally centered marked-coupling repair remains open, and no global frontier formula is asserted.

project_justification.gap: The closest published work gives the binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity endpoints and explicitly leaves maximal-radius dependence unresolved.  The accepted same-class parent gives a nonmatching bracket; the present results close the additional union \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\) for \(d\le n\), but not the remaining radius-dependent wedge.
project_justification.niche: Unknown random cell masses, unknown overlapping propensities, empty cells, supportwise centering around the ATE, and only conditional second moments make the residual converse neither fixed-design shrinkage nor a routine polynomial-functional problem.  The corrected residual wedge additionally enforces \(u_{n,d}>n^{-1}\), so already-closed approximation-scale points are excluded.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a total empirical-mass estimator, proves collision-scale minimax risk on the union of the empirical and rare-cell approximation regions, and proves a full-mixture obstruction for the displayed benchmark prior.  For lower-bound transfer, the published binary anchor embeds in the present real-outcome class through \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\), which scales ATEs and squared risks by \(M\) and \(M^2\).  For the real-outcome upper bound, the declared envelopes imply \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\).  The precisely specified conditionally centered shared-design converse remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, revised 2026) provide the binary-outcome baseline in Theorems 2--4; Section 4.2 identifies the unresolved radius dependence and discusses extension under bounded conditional second moments.  Their binary anchor transfers into the present centered real-outcome class by \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\): conditional means then lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\), conditional central variances are at most \(M^2/4\), ATE separations scale by \(M\), and squared-error lower bounds scale by \(M^2\).  Conversely, the real-outcome upper analysis uses only \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\), not bounded outcomes.  Section 7's 401(k) eligibility and net-assets analysis is the consumer but does not validate overlap or its reported intervals.  The internal accepted parent supplies the same-class bracket and the channel and factorial-lift obstructions.  The approximation and mixture architectures are informed by Zeng et al.'s cited polynomial-functional literature, but none of those sources resolves exact normalization, self-centering, or supportwise radius here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: A hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer gives only product-scale separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering at \(\sigma=0\).  The explicit family \(\Pi_h^\star\) further shows that exact normalization, identical design marginals, supportwise radius, and separated ATEs are not sufficient: its hypothesis-wide outcome shift yields a sign test with total variation tending to one at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\).  The newly closed approximation branch removes every \(d\le n\) point with \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\) from the residual problem.  Any replacement converse must operate in the corrected wedge, eliminate the globally visible first-order coefficient, and control the full marked likelihood.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Consistency and exchangeability identify the displayed ATE.  The established claims are the empirical-mass risk bound, the refined infimum-risk bracket, collision-scale minimax risk for \(2\le d\le n\) whenever \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), and failure of the displayed benchmark global-shift prior.  The open domain \(\mathcal W\) now requires \(n^{-1}<u_{n,d}<1\) in addition to \(d>n\) or \(\sigma^2d^2>n\); the benchmark marked-prior repair remains open inside that domain.  No global sharp rate, unspecified selector, unknown-radius adaptation, confidence interval, bounded-outcome assumption, overlap validation, or claim about the reported 401(k) intervals is included.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem-level result combines two independently evaluable sufficient conditions: the empirical-mass branch \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) and the inherited approximation branch \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\).
statement_notes.gap: The accepted parent leaves radius-dependent gaps, but its \(u_{n,d}\) upper branch and the empirical-mass correction together already close this full union at the collision scale.
statement_notes.consumer: For sparse adjustment tables, the result specifies when a calibrated near-homogeneity assumption is sufficient for parametric-order ATE estimation; it does not claim necessity outside the proved union.

statement_notes.justification: This isolates the first converse calculation after removing both the empirical region and the already-closed \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\) approximation region.
statement_notes.gap: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), neither closed-region condition holds.  The outer separation bracket remains logarithmically nonmatching, and the conditionally centered marked-score program is not specified tightly enough to decide whether super-parametric separation is feasible.
statement_notes.consumer: A benchmark construction passing normalization, realization-wise radius, target concentration, and full-mixture distance would justify extending a rare-cell converse into the corrected residual wedge; a universal parametric obstruction would rule out that architecture.
